regimeSub: Brent punches $99 on resumed Iran tensions; BOK hikes to 3% as Fed September decision looms.
themes: US-Iran conflict escalation drives Brent to $99.32 (+2.3% from yesterday's $97.13) → OPEC+ Sep 6 decision to hold production steady amplifies supply squeeze; Hormuz premium fully embedded
BOK hikes 25bp to 3.0% (Korea Herald Sep 7) → won strengthens to 1338 from 1339; KOSPI -0.4% to 7102 as tightening cycle weighs on domestic sentiment despite HBM tailwinds
Fed outlook murky: Waller 'muddied' Sep hike path (PBS Sep 4) while Warsh maintains hawkish bias on 3.3% CPI; August NFP +162K vs ~100K keeping Sep hike as base case; 10Y at 4.78% (+1bp)
Gold retreats to $4426 (-0.9% from $4468) as real rates hold at 1.48%; haven demand moderates despite geopolitical risk as hawkish Fed pricing dominates short-term flows

headline: Brent breaches $99 as US-Iran tensions reignite and OPEC+ holds steady, while BOK's third consecutive hike to 3% and Waller's muddied Fed guidance leave markets bracing for September volatility.
